subject: Media Literacy
title: Cinema: Stories on the Big Screen
description: Learn Cinema: Stories on the Big Screen in one minute.

hook.text: In 1895, audiences screamed and ducked when the Lumière Brothers showed a train arriving on screen.

buildup.text: Cinema combined photography, sound, and narrative into the most immersive medium yet.

discovery.text: Hollywood became a global factory of culture, exporting American values to every continent.

twist.text: Governments quickly realized cinema's propaganda power — from Nazi films to wartime newsreels.

climax.text: Film taught the world to think in stories — beginnings, middles, and emotionally satisfying endings.

punchline.text: Cinema didn't just show reality. It taught us how to feel about it.

quiz.question: Why was cinema a powerful tool for propaganda?
options: It combined visuals, sound, and narrative for emotional impact
It could only be shown once
